text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police chief, Inspector General Ibrahim Coomasie says investigations have shown conclusively that opposition NADECO group is behind recent bomb attacks in Nigeria.
- Scandal involving officials taking bribes to issue visas rocks British embassy in Lagos; London's Scotland Yard police called in to investigate.
- Ships sail into Lagos with 53 million litres of fuel from Port Harcourt refinery in southeast after state oil firm NNPC resolves dispute with port authority that caused fuel shortage.
- Federal government disburses 53 million naira to exporters as incentive for them to agggresively promote their wares.
- Formal commissioning of export processing zone in Calabar, southeast due this quarter may have been postponed by a year to allow for dredging of new port in the area.
- Oil minister Dan Etete sets up two groups to monitor operations of Nigeria's joint ventures with multinational oil firms and to oversee $4 billion liquefied natural gas project.
- Customs says it dismissed 1,042 last year and will change its uniform to give the department a new image.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani says Nigeria can repay its foreign debt within 10 years if it gets debt relief that is due to it for implementing its economic programme.
- Top management changes at United Bank for Africa, one of Nigeria's top three as chairman and chief executive officer retire and are succeeded by their deputies.
